#function compute CWD

fcwd_et <- function(cwd, ppt, aet, wmy, month, min_aet = 40, throughfall = 1,
                    reset_wmy = TRUE, min_cwd = -1000) {
  # ppt: monthly precipitation
  # eat: evapotranspiration (actual or climatological)
  # wmy: wettest month of the year
  # min_et: minimum ET threshold to avoid unrealistically low ET
  # throughfall: fraction of ppt that contributes to water balance
  # reset_wmy: logical, reset CWD at wettest month
  # min_cwd: lower bound for cumulative deficit

  n <- length(ppt)           # number of months in the series
  cwd[1] <- 0                # initial CWD: first month starts at zero

  for (i in 2:n) {           # loop from month 2 to end
    # accumulate CWD: previous month's deficit + current month's water balance
    cwd[i] <- cwd[i - 1] + (throughfall * ppt[i]) - max(aet[i], min_aet, na.rm = TRUE)

    # reset CWD to zero if this is the wettest month
    if (reset_wmy) {
      if (i <= length(wmy) && month[i] == wmy[i]) cwd[i] <- 0
    }

    # impose lower bound: deficit cannot exceed min_cwd
    cwd[i] <- max(cwd[i], min_cwd)
  }

  return(cwd)                # return the full CWD vector
}
  setorder(clim_all, plot, year, month)
  
  clim_all[, cwd := fcwd_et(cwd, ppt, aet, wmy, month)]

  #get mean and sigma of all months for this period
  
  clim_stats <- clim_all[year >= 1981 & year <= 2010][, .(
    mean_tmax = mean(tmax),
    sd_tmax   = sd(tmax),
    mean_vpd  = mean(vpd),
    sd_vpd    = sd(vpd),
    mean_srad = mean(srad),
    sd_srad   = sd(srad),
    mean_cwd = mean(cwd, na.rm=TRUE),
    sd_cwd   = sd(cwd, na.rm=TRUE),
    mean_tmean = mean(tmean, na.rm=TRUE),
    sd_tmean   = sd(tmean, na.rm=TRUE)
  ), by = c("plot", "month")]

  clim_all <- merge(clim_all, clim_stats, by = c("plot", "month"), all.x = TRUE)

  ## ---- standardize: standardized anomalies (z-scores) to account for the natural variability of each plot.
  clim_all[, `:=`(
    z_tmax = (tmax - mean_tmax) / sd_tmax,
    z_vpd  = (vpd  - mean_vpd)  / sd_vpd,
    z_srad = (srad - mean_srad) / sd_srad,
    z_cwd  = (cwd  - mean_cwd)  / sd_cwd,
    z_tmean = (tmean - mean_tmean) / sd_tmean
  )]
  
  #Set intervals to match inventories years with mean(or max) climate anomaly
  
obs_site_wide <- obs_site_wide[order(subplot, year)]

obs_site_wide[, interval := .GRP, by = .(subplot, year)] #groups the data by subplot × year. it gives the group number in the order groups appear
obs_site_wide[, year_end := shift(year, type = "lead"), by = subplot] #for each subplot, year_end is the next census year
obs_site_wide[is.na(year_end), year_end := max(year), by=subplot] #The last year per subplot has no “next” year = NA. NA is replaced by max year
obs_site_wide[, interval := paste0(year, "_", year_end)]


intervals <- obs_site_wide[, .(subplot, plot, interval, year_start = year, year_end)]

# start and end year on climate data
clim_all[, `:=`(year_start = year, year_end = year)]

setkey(intervals, plot, year_start, year_end)
setkey(clim_all, plot, year_start, year_end)

# 3️⃣ Perform the non-equi join
clim_all_interval <- foverlaps(
  clim_all,       # x #For each climate year, find the inventory interval it belongs to
  intervals,      # y
  by.x = c("plot", "year_start", "year_end"),
  by.y = c("plot", "year_start", "year_end"),
  type = "within",  # keep climate years inside interval
nomatch = 0L      # drop climate years outside any interval
  )


  ## ---- aggregate per census
census_anom <- clim_all_interval[, .(
  mean_z_tmax  = mean(z_tmax, na.rm = TRUE),
  max_z_tmax   = max(z_tmax,  na.rm = TRUE),
  mean_tmax   = mean(tmax,  na.rm = TRUE),

  mean_z_vpd   = mean(z_vpd,  na.rm = TRUE),
  max_z_vpd    = max(z_vpd,   na.rm = TRUE),
  mean_vpd   = mean(vpd,  na.rm = TRUE),

  
  mean_z_srad  = mean(z_srad, na.rm = TRUE),
  max_z_srad   = max(z_srad,  na.rm = TRUE),
  mean_srad   = mean(srad,  na.rm = TRUE),

  mean_z_cwd   = mean(z_cwd,  na.rm = TRUE),
  max_z_cwd    = max(z_cwd,   na.rm = TRUE),
  mean_cwd    = mean(cwd,   na.rm = TRUE)
), by = .(plot, interval)]#For each plot and census year, average all monthly anomalies that were labeled with that census year. ex: year_bin = 1985, all months from all years from 1982–1985 are averaged (if let's say the last inventory year - year_bin was 1981)

Generate model residuals with BAM

#agb gain (agb_growth + agb_recr)

Code 
cols <- c("max_z_tmax", 
          "mean_z_vpd", 
          "mean_z_srad", 
          "mean_z_cwd")

merged <- merged %>%
  mutate(
    plot = as.factor(plot),
    subplot = as.factor(subplot),
    treatment = as.factor(treatment),
    interval_num = as.numeric(sub("_.*", "", interval)),
    agb_gain = agb_growth + agb_recr,
    dagb = agb_growth + agb_recr - agb_mort
  ) %>%
  group_by(site) %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(cols), ~ as.numeric(scale(.)))) %>%
  ungroup()

setDT(merged)

site_models <- list()


for (s in sites) {
  merged_site <- merged[site == s]
  site_models[[s]] <- list()
  
  AR <- ave(merged_site$interval_num, merged_site$subplot, FUN = function(x) x == min(x)) |> as.logical()#TRUE for the first census year per subplot

    # choose k based on unique years
  
  ny <- uniqueN(merged_site$interval_num)

  k_use <- fifelse(ny <= 20, 3,
          fifelse(ny <= 25, 5, 7))
  
  cat("Site:", s, "- unique years:", uniqueN(merged_site$interval_num), "- k used:", k_use, "\n")
  
    # ---- 1) baseline model (NO AR) - used to estimate rho
  m0 <- bam(
    agb_gain ~
      s(interval_num, k = k_use) +
      s(treatment, bs = "re") +
      s(subplot, bs = "re") +
      s(interval_num, subplot, bs = "fs", k = k_use),#continuous and categorical variable
    data = merged_site,
    discrete = FALSE
  )
  

mf0 <- model.frame(m0)

res0 <- resid(m0, type = "response")

# Compute lag-1 autocorrelation for each subplot separately

acf_list <- lapply(split(res0, mf0$subplot), function(x) {
  if(length(x) < 3) return(NA_real_)
  acf(x, plot = FALSE)$acf[2]
})

# Pick the largest absolute lag-1 among all subplots for the site
# This ensures that rho0 captures the strongest temporal correlation present
rho0 <- max(abs(unlist(acf_list)), na.rm = TRUE)
rho0 <- max(min(rho0, 0.8), 0)

  cat("  estimated rho:", round(rho0, 3), "\n")
  

  # fit BAM
    mod <- bam(
      agb_gain ~ s(interval_num, k = k_use)+ 
        s(treatment, bs="re") +
                   s(subplot, bs="re") +
                   s(interval_num, subplot, bs="fs", k=k_use),
      data = merged_site,
      rho = rho0, 
      AR.start = AR,
      discrete = F#T is for very large datasets, some accuracy is traded for speed
    )
  
  res <- residuals(mod, type="response")
  
mf <- model.frame(mod)

acf_res <- tapply(
  res,
  mf$subplot,
  function(x) {
    if (length(x) < 3) return(NULL)
    acf(x, plot = FALSE)
  }
)  
      site_models[[s]]<- list(
      model = mod,
      rho = rho0,
      residuals = res,
      acf = acf_res
    )
      
#print(acf_res)[[s]]#Mbaiki: residuals 10 years apart are still correlated at ~0.59.lag-1 = consecutive censuses, lag-2 = two censuses apart

}
  


res_plot <- rbindlist(
  lapply(names(site_models), function(s) {
    df_site <- merged[site == s]
    
    # only rows used in BAM
    used <- !is.na(df_site$agb_gain)
    
    data.table(
      site = s,
      interval_num = df_site$interval_num[used],
      subplot = df_site$subplot[used],
      residual = site_models[[s]]$residuals
    )
  })
)

Plot BAM

Code 
# ==========================================================
# 1. EXTRACT PREDICTIONS PER SITE (ON RESPONSE SCALE)
# ==========================================================

smooth_list <- list()
raw_list <- list()

for (s in names(site_models)) {
  
  mod <- site_models[[s]]$model
  
  # Original model data
  dat <- model.frame(mod)
  
  dat$treatment <- as.factor(dat$treatment)
  dat$subplot   <- as.factor(dat$subplot)
  
  # Store raw data for plotting
  raw_df <- dat %>%
    mutate(site = s)
  
  raw_list[[s]] <- raw_df
  
  # Prediction grid across interval range
  newdata <- data.frame(
    interval_num = seq(
      min(dat$interval_num),
      max(dat$interval_num),
      length.out = 100
    ),
    treatment = levels(dat$treatment),
    subplot   = dat$subplot[1]     # arbitrary level
  )
  
  newdata$treatment <- factor(newdata$treatment,
                            levels = levels(dat$treatment))

newdata$subplot <- factor(newdata$subplot,
                          levels = levels(dat$subplot))
  
  # Predict full response (AGB gain) including intercept and smooths
  pred <- predict(
    mod,
    newdata = newdata,
    type = "response",
    se.fit = TRUE
  )
  
  # Build dataframe
  df_smooth <- data.frame(
    site = s,
    interval_num = newdata$interval_num,
    fit = pred$fit,
    se  = pred$se.fit, 
    treatment=newdata$treatment
  )
  
  smooth_list[[s]] <- df_smooth
}

# Combine all sites
smooth_df <- bind_rows(smooth_list)
raw_df_all <- bind_rows(raw_list)

# ==========================================================
# 2. PLOT RAW DATA + SMOOTH
# ==========================================================

p <- ggplot() +
  
  # Raw points
  geom_point(
    data = raw_df_all,
    aes(x = interval_num, y = agb_gain),
    alpha = 0.4,
    size = 1.5
  ) +
  
  # Smooth line (predicted AGB gain)
  geom_line(
    data = smooth_df,
    aes(x = interval_num, y = fit),
    linewidth = 1,
    color = "blue"
  ) +
  
  # 95% confidence ribbon
  geom_ribbon(
    data = smooth_df,
    aes(
      x = interval_num,
      ymin = fit - 2 * se,
      ymax = fit + 2 * se
    ),
    alpha = 0.2,
    fill = "blue"
  ) +
  
  facet_wrap(~ site+treatment, scales = "free_y") +
  
  labs(
    x = "Interval",
    y = "agb_gain",
    title = "Observed dagb with site-specific BAM smooth (AR1)"
  ) +
  
  theme_minimal()

print(p)

causal inference framework:

#We can test for total causal effects (TCE) and/or direct causal effects (DCE). #TCEs include all downstream variables (e.g., the effect of Tmax on agb gain, including it’s effect via VPD, etc). #DCEs include direct causal pathways only (e.g., the effect of Tmax on agb gain, excluding it’s effect via VPD).

mf0 <- model.frame(m0)

acf_list <- lapply(split(res0, mf0$subplot), function(x) {

})

# Pick the largest absolute lag-1 among all subplots for the site

rho0 <- max(abs(unlist(acf_list)), na.rm = TRUE)
rho0 <- max(min(rho0, 0.8), 0)

  cat("  estimated rho:", round(rho0, 3), "\n")

  mod3 <- bam(

acf_res <- tapply(

  smooth_tab3 <- broom::tidy(mod3, parametric = FALSE) %>% mutate(Term_type = "smooth")
  tab_mod3    <- bind_rows(param_tab3, smooth_tab3) %>%

#Tmax - DCE

Code 
#cor.test(merged$mean_z_tmax, merged$mean_z_srad)#confirm srad is a confounder 

site_models2<- list()

table_results_combined <- list()

for (s in sites) {
  merged_site <- merged[site == s]
  
  # choose k based on unique years
    ny <- uniqueN(merged_site$interval_num)

  k_use <- fifelse(ny <= 20, 3,
          fifelse(ny <= 25, 5, 7))
  
  cat("Site:", s, "- unique years:", uniqueN(merged_site$interval_num), "- k used:", k_use, "\n")

  
  AR <- ave(merged_site$interval_num, merged_site$subplot, FUN = function(x) x == min(x)) |> as.logical()

    # ---- 1) baseline model (NO AR) - used to estimate rho
  m0 <- bam(
    agb_gain ~
      s(interval_num, k = k_use) +
      s(treatment, bs = "re") +
      s(subplot, bs = "re") +
      s(interval_num, subplot, bs = "fs", k = k_use)+
          mean_z_tmax:treatment+mean_z_srad+mean_z_vpd+mean_z_cwd,#here we block the effect of vpd and cwd
    data = merged_site,
    discrete = FALSE
  )
  
mf0 <- model.frame(m0)

res0 <- resid(m0, type = "response")

# Compute lag-1 autocorrelation for each subplot separately

acf_list <- lapply(split(res0, mf0$subplot), function(x) {
  if(length(x) < 3) return(NA_real_)
  acf(x, plot = FALSE)$acf[2]
})

# Pick the largest absolute lag-1 among all subplots for the site
# This ensures that rho0 captures the strongest temporal correlation present
rho0 <- max(abs(unlist(acf_list)), na.rm = TRUE)
rho0 <- max(min(rho0, 0.8), 0)

  cat("  estimated rho:", round(rho0, 3), "\n")

    # fit BAM 
  mod3 <- bam(
    agb_gain ~ 
      s(interval_num, k = k_use) +
      s(treatment, bs="re") +
      s(subplot, bs="re")+
      s(interval_num, subplot, bs="fs", k=k_use)+
          mean_z_tmax:treatment+mean_z_srad+mean_z_vpd+mean_z_cwd,
    data = merged_site,
    rho = rho0,
    AR.start = AR,
    discrete = FALSE
  )
  
  #
  
  #plot(mod3, select=1)

  res <- residuals(mod3, type="response")
  
mf <- model.frame(mod3)

acf_res <- tapply(
  res,
  mf$subplot,
  function(x) {
    if (length(x) < 3) return(NULL)
    acf(x, plot = FALSE)
  }
)  
      site_models2[[s]]<- list(
      model = mod3,
      rho = rho0,
      residuals = res,
      acf = acf_res
    )    
      
  param_tab3  <- broom::tidy(mod3, parametric = TRUE) %>% mutate(Term_type = "parametric")
  smooth_tab3 <- broom::tidy(mod3, parametric = FALSE) %>% mutate(Term_type = "smooth")
  tab_mod3    <- bind_rows(param_tab3, smooth_tab3) %>%
                    mutate(Model_type = "BAM_re",
                           Model = s)
  
 
  # ---- combine both models for this site ----
  table_results_combined[[s]] <- bind_rows(tab_mod3)
}

Code 
site_models2<- list()

table_results_combined <- list()

for (s in sites) {
  merged_site <- merged[site == s]
  
  # choose k based on unique years
    ny <- uniqueN(merged_site$interval_num)

  k_use <- fifelse(ny <= 20, 3,
          fifelse(ny <= 25, 5, 7))
  
  cat("Site:", s, "- unique years:", uniqueN(merged_site$interval_num), "- k used:", k_use, "\n")

  
  AR <- ave(merged_site$interval_num, merged_site$subplot, FUN = function(x) x == min(x)) |> as.logical()

    # ---- 1) baseline model (NO AR) - used to estimate rho
  m0 <- bam(
    agb_gain ~
      s(interval_num, k = k_use) +
      s(treatment, bs = "re") +
      s(subplot, bs = "re") +
      s(interval_num, subplot, bs = "fs", k = k_use)+
          mean_z_srad:treatment+mean_z_vpd+mean_z_tmax+mean_z_cwd,
    data = merged_site,
    discrete = FALSE
  )
  
mf0 <- model.frame(m0)

res0 <- resid(m0, type = "response")

# Compute lag-1 autocorrelation for each subplot separately

acf_list <- lapply(split(res0, mf0$subplot), function(x) {
  if(length(x) < 3) return(NA_real_)
  acf(x, plot = FALSE)$acf[2]
})

# Pick the largest absolute lag-1 among all subplots for the site
# This ensures that rho0 captures the strongest temporal correlation present
rho0 <- max(abs(unlist(acf_list)), na.rm = TRUE)
rho0 <- max(min(rho0, 0.8), 0)

  cat("  estimated rho:", round(rho0, 3), "\n")

    # fit BAM 
  mod3 <- bam(
    agb_gain ~ 
      s(interval_num, k = k_use) +
      s(treatment, bs="re") +
      s(subplot, bs="re")+
      s(interval_num, subplot, bs="fs", k=k_use)+
          mean_z_srad:treatment+mean_z_vpd+mean_z_tmax+mean_z_cwd,
    data = merged_site,
    rho = rho0,
    AR.start = AR,
    discrete = FALSE
  )
  
  #
  
  #plot(mod3, select=1)

  res <- residuals(mod3, type="response")
  
mf <- model.frame(mod3)

acf_res <- tapply(
  res,
  mf$subplot,
  function(x) {
    if (length(x) < 3) return(NULL)
    acf(x, plot = FALSE)
  }
)  
      site_models2[[s]]<- list(
      model = mod3,
      rho = rho0,
      residuals = res,
      acf = acf_res
    )    
      
  param_tab3  <- broom::tidy(mod3, parametric = TRUE) %>% mutate(Term_type = "parametric")
  smooth_tab3 <- broom::tidy(mod3, parametric = FALSE) %>% mutate(Term_type = "smooth")
  tab_mod3    <- bind_rows(param_tab3, smooth_tab3) %>%
                    mutate(Model_type = "BAM_re",
                           Model = s)
  
 
  # ---- combine both models for this site ----
  table_results_combined[[s]] <- bind_rows(tab_mod3)
}

#CWM WD effects

Code 
mod_use <- site_models2[["Paracou"]]$model   

merged_site <- merged[site == "Paracou"]

# ranges
vpd_seq <- seq(
  min(merged_site$mean_z_vpd, na.rm=TRUE),
  max(merged_site$mean_z_vpd, na.rm=TRUE),
  length.out = 100
)

# choose WD levels (mean ± 1 SD)
wd_mean <- mean(merged_site$WD_cwm_ba, na.rm=TRUE)
wd_sd   <- sd(merged_site$WD_cwm_ba, na.rm=TRUE)

wd_levels <- c(wd_mean - 3*wd_sd,
               wd_mean,
               wd_mean + 3*wd_sd)



newdat <- expand.grid(
  mean_z_vpd = vpd_seq,
  WD_cwm_ba   = wd_levels,
  mean_z_srad = mean(merged_site$mean_z_srad, na.rm=TRUE),
    mean_z_tmax = mean(merged_site$mean_z_tmax, na.rm=TRUE),
  interval_num = mean(merged_site$interval_num, na.rm=TRUE),
  treatment = levels(merged_site$treatment),
  subplot   = levels(merged_site$subplot)
)


newdat$pred <- predict(
  mod_use,
  newdata = newdat,
  type = "response",
  exclude = c("s(subplot)", "s(interval_num,subplot)")
)

ggplot(newdat,
       aes(x = mean_z_vpd,
           y = pred,
           color = factor(WD_cwm_ba))) +
  geom_line(size = 1.2) +
    facet_wrap(~ treatment) +
  labs(color = "WD (mean ± SD)",
       x = "vpd anomaly",
       y = "Predicted AGB gain") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)
